body.reply:
No. With both majors, the planner's last term is Spring 2030, so it doesn't finish by Spring 2028. Data Science alone doesn't make Spring 2028 either. Its last term is Fall 2028.

- Data Science alone: the plan ends Fall 2028 with CS 163 [1], MATH 167R [2], MATH 32 [3] and PHIL 133 [4].
- Adding Economics: you still need ECON 1B [5] and the rest of the Economics core, including ECON 100W [6], ECON 103A [7], ECON 101 [8], ECON 102 [9], ECON 103B [10] and ECON 104 [11]. You also need the upper-division electives, such as ECON 106 [12] and ECON 135 [13]. Those push the plan to Spring 2030.
- The plan covers only major requirements in the curated catalog data. It doesn't cover General Education, total units, residency or the graduation application.
- Not scheduled: Data Science Domain Field Electives, 9 units that need prior department approval [14]. The planner can't place them, and the finish term doesn't include them.
- Caveats: the catalog is from 2025-2026 and wasn't checked against 2026-2027. The planner assumes every course is offered in both Fall and Spring [15][16]. CS 22A counts only with department approval [17].

Confirm with your advisor. Here's a question you can ask them:
“Can any Economics, B.S. courses count toward the 9 units of Data Science Domain Field Electives, and can CS 22A count with department approval? Is there any way to finish both majors by Spring 2028?”
